doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: School plays and a woman impression
summary: He had bit parts in school plays, including doing a comic woman impression, the extent of his vaudeville life.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Were you known, like in school, did you and your brother or your sister have this kind of like reputation as entertainers?

No not really. Not in the school. Except like I had bit parts in school plays, like as a bird or something, sitting on a desk with bird crap on. But never any for what I wanted to be. And I think I was too early in the music scene. But they did select me for these plays, to do something. You know one play they had me doing — what is this guy called — Flip Phillips, when he did that woman thing, that girl thing?
Yeah. He’s a comedian. Well anyhow he does this imitation of a woman.
And you got to do that?
I got to do one of those impressions, uncomfortably, because I think they put high heels on me and I’m wiggling. But that was the extent of my vaudevillian life.
